newsitem.title: USA: Weather expert sees active hurricane season in '97.
newsitem.headline: Weather expert sees active hurricane season in '97.

text.p: A Colorado State University hurricane researcher said the 1997 hurricane season will see slightly above-average activity with seven hurricanes, of which three will become major hurricanes.
Researcher William Gray said 1997 would be the third consecutive season of "above average hurricane formation" and 1995 through 1997 would be the most active three-year hurricane span in history.
Gray and his colleagues are predicting 11 tropical storms between June 1 and November 30, the hurricane season.
Of the 11 storms, seven will evolve into hurricanes and three will turn into major hurricanes with winds topping 111 miles per hour, Gray said in a statement.
On average, 9.3 tropical storms, 5.8 hurricanes and 2.1 major hurricanes form annually, Gray said.

Gray noted that his forecast for 1996 season of 11 tropical storms with seven forming hurricanes and three intense hurricanes fell short. The 1996 season saw 13 tropical storms and nine hurricanes, six of them intense, Gray said.
Gray and his research team at the university study wind, rainfall, temperature, and atmospheric pressure to devise forecasts.
